pinterest.title: Baltic Wedding Traditions: Three Countries, Three Sets of Customs
pinterest.description: Baltic wedding traditions are really three national traditions. Latvia keeps mičošana, a midnight ritual often led by folklore groups. Lithuania welcomes newlyweds with bread and salt and once removed the bride's rue wreath in gaubtuvės. Estonia recorded tanutamine, when the bride was dressed as a married woman. Our guide takes each country in turn, for Australian couples planning in the Baltics or at home.

pinterest.title: Mičošana: The Midnight Latvian Wedding Ritual From Bride to Wife
pinterest.description: At modern Latvian weddings, mičošana is a midnight ritual in which the bride symbolically says goodbye to her status as a daughter and takes on the role of a wife. It is often led by folklore groups who sing the songs and perform the ritual. Plan it as a fixed midnight moment in your run sheet, and ask early whether a folklore group can perform. More Latvian wedding traditions in our guide.

pinterest.title: Tanutamine: The Estonian Wedding Bonnet Ceremony Explained
pinterest.description: In Estonian wedding tradition, tanutamine was the high point of the day: the bride was dressed in the garments of a married woman and became a young wife. The bonnet (tanu) was put on three times, then an apron was tied on. It was mostly done out of sight of the guests, so plan it today as a private or semi-private moment. Read the full guide to Estonian, Latvian and Lithuanian customs.

slides: Baltic wedding traditions you did not know: three countries, three sets of customs
Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania each have their own language and customs. A "Baltic" wedding is really one of three national traditions.
Latvia: mičošana. A midnight ritual, often led by folklore groups, in which the bride says goodbye to her status as a daughter and takes on the role of wife.
Latvia: at modern weddings guests still shout "Rūgts!" (bitter), and the couple are expected to kiss.
Lithuania: newlyweds have long been welcomed as the most honoured guests, with bread and salt and a drink.
Lithuania: gaubtuvės, the removal of the bride's rue wreath, was one of the most important old wedding rites.
Estonia: tanutamine. The bride was dressed as a married woman, the bonnet (tanu) put on three times, then an apron tied on.
